thread:
Sam: FYI Acme support just escalated: dedicated-west pool showing ~30% throughput loss and a spike in 429s since ~08:12 UTC. High tail latency reported.
Isha: looked at the metrics at 08:15 — autoscaler did not add nodes, pool GPU util ~84% but queue length steadily climbing. No recent deploys.
Devon: flagging packing/continuous-batcher as likely culprits. We pushed a runtime change last night that reduced max_pack_tokens for rwd-llama-70b-q8 on a canary. Could be causing premature flushes.
Maya: which change/commit? did canary show any regressions?
Devon: commit a8f3c29 changed scheduler.pack_tokens from 8192 -> 4096 for memory safety. Canary traffic looked fine (short prompts) but Acme uses long system prompts + appended embeddings.
Sam: customer confirms avg request length increased over the past week (they concatenated embedding vectors into prompts). That would push batches over the token cap and force early drains.
OpsBot: alert: pool=dedicated-west queue_depth=410 avg_batch_size=2.1 avg_tokens_per_batch=3700 qps=172
Isha: avg_batch_size ~2 is killing throughput.
Devon: repro locally with a synthetic mix resembling Acme. Script:
```
./dev/stress_test --pool=dedicated-west --model=rwd-llama-70b-q8 --qps=180 --prompt-mix=acme_long
```
Sample output from repro:
```
qps:180 inflight:140 avg_batch:2.2 tokens_per_batch:3650 p99:730ms
pack_efficiency:30% small_batches:11800
```
Maya: pack_efficiency 30% matches the low GPU throughput despite high queue backlog.
Devon: note we also lowered continuous_batcher.max_wait_ms from 12ms -> 5ms in the same runtime patch to reduce tail latency for short prompts. Combined with the lower token cap, this creates many tiny micro-batches.
Jordan: any autoscaler misconfig? why didn't it scale if GPU util was high?
Isha: autoscaler uses sustained GPU util >90% for 5m threshold; we were at 84-86% so it didn't trigger. But inefficiency means more nodes wouldn't help until packing improves.
Sam: customer also flagged billing: cost per-response jumped because fewer tokens are packed per batch. They're worried about an overcharge window.
Maya: propose short-term mitigations: 1) roll back pack_tokens to 8192 for dedicated-west Acme-tagged pool; 2) increase continuous_batcher.max_wait_ms to 15ms on that pool; 3) enable fallback routing to a quantized variant if available.
Devon: hotfix steps (I will run):
1) set runtime flag on pool tag: runtime.scheduler.pack_tokens=8192 (rolling update)
2) feature-flag set continuous_batcher.max_wait_ms=15 for dedicated-west-acme
3) update route fallback: `api update-route --customer acme --fallback rwd-llama-70b-q4`
Maya: I'll coordinate the router rolling restart across the three router instances. ETA ~15m.
Sam: I'll inform support and Acme: "We are applying a temporary runtime adjustment to improve pack efficiency and latency. Expect improvements within ~30 minutes. We're also investigating billing impact." :white_check_mark:
Devon: after applying flags and rolling router, I re-ran repro:
```
qps:180 inflight:140 avg_batch:6.5 tokens_per_batch:4200 p99:270ms
pack_efficiency:78% small_batches:420
```
Jordan: p99 dropped from ~730ms -> ~270ms. Great.
Isha: any collateral impact on other tenants sharing the pool?
Devon: there are a few mid-tier tenants but their avg prompt length is smaller; revert should be neutral or slightly beneficial.
Jordan: follow-ups to add: 1) gate pack token changes behind canary routing for longer prompt mixes; 2) alert: pack_efficiency < 50% should trigger an ops alert; 3) link runtime/scheduler changes to the PR description so oncall can see risk.
Devon: created INF-4287 with logs, repro commands, and recommended defaults: `pack_tokens=8192`, `continuous_batcher.max_wait_ms=10-20`.
Isha: billing ops — flagging potential overbill window 08:12-08:45 UTC. We'll review invoices and offer credit if needed.
Maya: rolling restart progress: router-a -> back up, queue depth 95; router-b -> back up, queue 40; router-c -> back up, pool stabilized qps 170 avg_batch 6.3.
OpsBot: event: router-rolling-restart started dedicated-west 08:40 UTC
Sam: posted update to Acme support thread and added incident board entry. We'll run a 1hr postmortem tomorrow.
Jordan: add a short autoscaler tuning note: consider lowering the sustained util threshold for dedicated pools with heavy-long-prompt customers or add pack_efficiency signal to trigger scale.
Sam: assigned actions: @Maya run rollout, @Devon apply runtime flags + validate with repro, @Isha lead customer comms & billing review, @Jordan own oncall follow-ups.
Maya: marking as in-progress and monitoring.
Sam: thanks everyone — good catch. Let's capture the timeline in the incident doc and follow up on gating and alerting improvements. :coffee:
